mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 0.5% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand offset by a nascent housing recovery, resulting in flat-to-slightly-positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -0.5% AND HOUST > previous 3-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not statistically greater than -2% at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.3 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depress corporate earnings expectations and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >0.3pp for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in economic activity, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not statistically less than zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary pressure regime, which increases risk premiums and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) above its 6-month moving average, with no corresponding rise in industrial production (INDPRO), signals a demand-side shift toward services and away from manufacturing, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to sector rotation into service-oriented equities.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 6-mo MA AND INDPRO <= 6-mo MA for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not statistically greater than zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) of at least 30,000 jobs for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >30,000 for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically greater than zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year decline in the GDP price index (GDPC1) of more than 2% combined with a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE change within ±0.1pp for three months) signals a demand-driven recession without significant labor market distress, which typically precedes a delayed but pronounced equity bear market over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND abs(UNRATE change) <= 0.1pp for 3 months
regime_hint: demand-driven recession with stable labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not statistically less than -2% at 5% significance.
